sentences.text:
This miscellaneous appeal by the claimants under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of award dated 22.11.2018 passed by Eighth Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
District Gwalior (hereinafter it would be referred to as ''the Claims Tribunal'') in Claim Case No.175/2017 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text:
Eighth Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
District Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability is not in dispute, however, the finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard is not in question.

As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of Prahalad, the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.9,87,500/- with interest @ 7% per annum from date of filing of application till its realization in favour of claimants.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19587 2 MA-1080-2019 Learned counsel for the appellants-claimants contends that the compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal accepting earning of deceased as Rs.5,000/- per month was inadequate looking to the fact that he was working as skilled Labour as "Mason" and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He also submits that income of deceased assessed by the Claims Tribunal is not just and proper.

Learned counsel for the appellants further submits that the compensation awarded by Claims Tribunal is on the lower side, therefore,
the claimants seek enhancement of compensation.

1

On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation amount after assessing the income of deceased.
Learned counsel for Insurance Company further submits that the cross-objection has already been filed.
Learned Claims Tribunal has committed an error in giving 30% future prospects in favour of claimants.

On relying the judgment passed in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi AIR 2017 SC 5157 , he submits that when age of the deceased was 40-50 years, then 25% of the income must be added in future prospects,
therefore, learned Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation but wrongly assessed future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

So far as the contention of learned counsel for the claimants that the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in holding the income of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19587 3 MA-1080-2019 deceased as Rs.5,000/-
per month, is concerned
, the appellants-claimants are unable to produce any substantial evidence with regard to prove the fact that the deceased was a skilled labour.
The appellants are also unable to prove monthly income of the deceased as Rs.20,000/- per month and they are unable to prove that deceased was skilled labour.

The Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of deceased as Rs.5,000/- per month, but according to the circular in regard to M.P.Minimum Wages Act, earning of unskilled labour would be Rs.6,950/-
per month.
So, in considered opinion of this Court, income of deceased as Rs.6950/- per month is just and proper for awarding compensation.

and the claimants are also entitled for compensation under future prospects and other conventional heads in the light of decisions of Apex Court in the cases of Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, AIR 2009 SC 3104 and National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi AIR 2017 SC 5157 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.
Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, 2020 SCC Online SC

sentences.text:
So far as the contention of learned counsel for Insurance Company that the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in awarding 30%
of income as future prospects is concerned, in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that if the deceased was not getting any fixed income, then 25% of income must be added towards future prospects considering the age of the deceased in between NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19587 4 MA-1080-2019 40-50 years.

The contention of learned counsel for claimants is that the Claims Tribunal has also committed in holding the age of deceased as 40 years is concerned, learned counsel placed reliance on the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of M. H Uma Maheshwari Vs. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. reported in 2020 (6) SCC 400 and Shashikala and Others Vs.
Gangalakshmamma and Another reported in 2015(2) ACC 76 and Smt. Manjesh Vs. Asgar Khan and Others.

sentences.text: wherein it has been held that when the age of the deceased was 45 years 05 months and 28 days, then the age of deceased should be adopted as 45 years and multiplier of 14 should be applied, therefore, in the present case, the multiplier of 15 should be applied considering the age of the deceased.

Smt. Saguna vs Ashok Sen on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97252536/
2
In the present case, the appellants-claimants are unable to produce any substantial evidence/documents in regard to prove the age of deceased.
Appellants/claimants are unable to prove the age of deceased below 40 years.
Therefore, the age of deceased must be assessed according to medical documents including postmoretem report (Ex.P-8) in which the age of the deceased has been specifically mentioned as 40 years.

So, in the light of the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) , the appellants-claimants should be entitled to get compensation towards future prospects to the extent of 25% in place of 30% as awarded by Claims Tribunal considering the age NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19587 5 MA-1080-2019 of deceased in between 40-50 years.

In view of aforesaid, the compensation awarded by learned Claims Tribunal is modified to the extent indicated under:-
 Heads compensation awarded  Income Rs.6950/- PM  Future Prospects 25% Rs.1738/-
 After loss of dependency (1/4th) Rs.2172/-
 Rs.6516/- (8688-2172)
 Annual Future Income  x 12M= 78,192  Total income Rs.11,72,880/-
 loss of consortium (wife, two Rs.2,42,000/- (48,400 x  children and parents) 5)
 Loss of estate, funeral expenses and  Rs.18150/-x 2= 36,300/-
 love and affection etc.
The learned Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.9,87,500/-.

Thus, the appellants/claimants are held entitled to receive enhanced amount of Rs.4,63,680/- in addition to the amount of compensation already awarded by learned Claims Tribunal, making the total compensation amount of Rs.14,51,180/-
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 7% per annum as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19587 6 MA-1080-2019 of appeal,
the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the claimants within four weeks' from today and proof thereof shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
Appeal stands allowed to the aforesaid extent and disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
